newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada temporarily recalls ambassador to Iran.
newsitem.headline: Canada temporarily recalls ambassador to Iran.

text.p: Canada said on Friday it recalled its ambassador to Iran for a few days of consultations after a Berlin court verdict that Iran ordered the killing of four dissidents.

"This verdict is being carefully reviewed by the Canadian government," Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy said in a statement. "It is not acceptable that Iran or any other country attack an opponent on foreign soil."
Axworthy said he was deeply concerned about Thursday's verdict, which implicated high-ranking Iranians in the killings of four Iranian Kurds in the Mykonos restaurant in Berlin in 1992.
Germany decided to expel four Iranian diplomats, and the European Union moved to recall ambassadors and break off "critical dialogue" with Iran.
Axworthy said Canada had been consulting with the European Union, the G7 and other partners about the crisis.
